doc.title: Luis Conte interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 24, 2025

title: Music as food for Cubans, and return visits 2009-2012
summary: Conte describes the hardship in Cuba today and how music is everywhere on the street, keeping people alive; a brief screen adjustment follows.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: Yeah. There’s a quote I read from you. “Music is almost like food to Cuban people” which I thought was a strong statement.

Yeah. You know the situation in Cuba is really hard, right at this moment, and it’s been for years. There’s the Communism thing and the whole bit of freedom and the embargo. And now it’s getting super worse. But I did go back to visit in 2009 and 2010 and 2012. And man, let me tell you these people, I mean they’re struggling but at one point I literally said okay, can everybody just be quiet for a second? Because you know you walk down, you’re either at the hotel, the restaurant, the Latin -- they’ve got like a killing samba band. This is in Santiago you know, playing son. Then you’re walking down the street and there’s a trio in the corner and they’re going on, and there’s a rumba happening, and then you’re walking down another street and like the radio is blasting. And this goes on, it’s food man, that’s how they keep alive man.
I’m going to ask you to move your screen so that you’re a little higher in the – yeah – that way the closed captions won’t cover your face.
Yeah that’s perfect, and then we’ll just edit this out.
